Topics · Hard times

Is my poor mother less honoured by God?

The Quran says No to wealth as honour and poverty as insult, honours all, and measures by mindfulness.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكْرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ١٥ وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّىٓ أَهَـٰنَنِ١٦ كَلَّا ۖ بَل لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ١٧ وَلَا تَحَـٰٓضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ١٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."[1918] But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." No![1919] But you do not honor the orphan And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.

Translator's notes

[1918] He is proud rather than grateful, attributing the favor to his own merit.

[1919] It is not like you imagine. Rather, Allāh tries people through prosperity and hardship and rewards both gratitude and patience with honor in the Hereafter.

Quran · Al-Fajr 89:15-18

Translation

Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me, lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is Yahweh?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.

Original · Hebrew

שָׁ֤וְא ׀ וּֽדְבַר־כָּזָ֡ב הַרְחֵ֬ק מִמֶּ֗נִּי רֵ֣אשׁ וָ֭עֹשֶׁר אַל־תִּֽתֶּן־לִ֑י הַ֝טְרִיפֵ֗נִי לֶ֣חֶם חֻקִּֽי׃ פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע ׀ וְכִחַשְׁתִּי֮ וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה וּפֶֽן־אִוָּרֵ֥שׁ וְגָנַ֑בְתִּי וְ֝תָפַ֗שְׂתִּי שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָֽי׃

Proverbs · 30:8-9

World English Bible

The verses describe a person who thinks that plenty means God has honoured him, and that narrowed provision means God has humiliated him. The answer is one flat word: No. The Quran does not accept money as the sign of God's love, or scarcity as the sign of His anger. Then it turns the question around: the fault lies in not honouring the orphan and not urging the feeding of the poor.

A question for you

What were you told about being poor?

If you sayThat it means little faith.
ThenThese verses answer that directly. The text does not link thin provision to thin faith.
If you sayThat it is a punishment.
ThenThat is exactly what the Quran refused when it said No. And this app does not call anyone's hardship a punishment.
If you sayNothing was said, but I feel ashamed.
ThenShame is a real feeling, but the verses do not make it God's verdict on you. The next step says what God says about you.

Translation of the meaning

And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.

Original · Hebrew

מָֽה־אֱנ֥וֹשׁ כִּֽי־תִזְכְּרֶ֑נּוּ וּבֶן־אָ֝דָ֗ם כִּ֣י תִפְקְדֶֽנּוּ׃ וַתְּחַסְּרֵ֣הוּ מְּ֭עַט מֵאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְכָב֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תְּעַטְּרֵֽהוּ׃ תַּ֭מְשִׁילֵהוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣י יָדֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֝ל שַׁ֣תָּה תַֽחַת־רַגְלָֽיו׃

the Psalms · 8:4-6

World English Bible

The verse says: We have honoured the children of Adam. All of them, in one phrase. The honour is given with creation itself, before anyone is asked about income. There is no exception in the sentence for those without savings. If someone tells you your worth depends on your wealth, this verse does not say so.

A question for you

What do you feel on hearing that the honour belongs to all people?

If you sayRelief.
ThenThat feeling belongs. Let it stay a while.
If you sayDoubt: is this for me too?
ThenThe phrase 'children of Adam' excludes no one. You are not asked to believe it today. Only to read it.
If you sayAnger at those who made me feel less.
ThenYour anger is understood. The verse stands with your dignity, not with those who insulted it.

Part 3 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَـٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَـٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous[1521] of you. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

Translator's notes

[1521] Literally, "he who has the most taqwā," i.e., consciousness and fear of Allāh, piety and righteousness.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:13

Translation

He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings,

Original · Ancient Greek

ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,

Acts · 17:26

World English Bible

The measure the verse gives: the noblest of you with God is the most mindful. Mindfulness: a person aware of God, with a conscience present. Not savings, not lineage, not titles. Your mother can have all of this as fully as anyone rich. Her prayers all those years are not erased by what is in her purse. The text does not measure her by what she lacks.

A question for you

How do you see your mother's prayer now?

If you sayAs something of worth to God.
ThenThat is what the verse says of the measure. No one judges but God.
If you sayWith pride mixed with pain.
ThenBoth are honest together. You need not choose.
If you saySome days I do not want to go on.
ThenThis app cannot hear you or reach anyone for you, so please do not carry this alone. Talk today to someone you trust, a doctor, or a helpline where you live, and if you are in danger now, reach for the nearest person who can help. Your dignity has not changed.

These reasonings do not cohere: I am richer than you, therefore I am better than you; I am more eloquent than you, therefore I am better than you. On the contrary, these rather cohere: I am richer than you, therefore my possessions are greater than yours; I am more eloquent than you, therefore my speech is superior to yours. But you are neither possession nor speech.
